t.3.56.1: Bṛhadaśva said: Having thus made a compact with Dvāpara, Kali then came to the place where that king of the Niṣadhas was.
t.3.56.2: Constantly watching for a weak spot, he dwelt for a long time among the Niṣadhas; then, in the twelfth year, Kali saw an opening in him.
t.3.56.3: Having passed urine and sipped water, the Naiṣadha sat down to the twilight worship without having cleansed his feet; there Kali entered into him.
t.3.56.4: Having entered into Nala, he went into the presence of Puṣkara and said this to Puṣkara: "Come, play at dice with Nala!"
t.3.56.5: For you, joined with me, will defeat Nala at the game of dice; having conquered King Nala, O king, take possession of the Niṣadhas.
t.3.56.6: Thus addressed by Kali, Puṣkara went up to Nala; and Kali too, becoming the bull among the cattle, went up to Puṣkara.
t.3.56.7: Having approached the heroic Nala, Puṣkara, his brother, the slayer of enemy heroes, said again and again, "Let us two play, with the bull as the stake!"
t.3.56.8: Then the high-minded king could not endure the challenge, and with Vaidarbhī looking on, he deemed it the time for staking a wager.
t.3.56.9: Then Nala, possessed by Kali, was defeated at the dice game and lost his gold and his wrought gold, his carriages and draught animals, and his garments.
t.3.56.10: But not one among his friends was able to restrain him, maddened as he was by the intoxication of dice, gambling on and bereft of his senses.
t.3.56.11: Then all the townspeople, together with the ministers, O Bhārata, came to see the afflicted king and to restrain him.
t.3.56.12: Then the charioteer approached Damayantī and informed her: "All these townspeople stand at the gate, having business to put before you."
t.3.56.14: Then Bhaimī, wasted by sorrow, her mind stricken with grief, spoke to the Naiṣadha in a voice choked with tears.
t.3.56.13: Let it be announced to the Naiṣadha that all the subjects, who discern dharma and artha, stand waiting here, unable to bear the misfortune of their king.
t.3.56.15: "O king, the citizens stand at the gate wishing to see you, together with all the ministers, led by their devotion to the king; you ought to see them." Thus she spoke again and again.
t.3.56.16: To her, the slender-waisted one with lovely eye-corners, lamenting thus, the king, possessed by Kali, said nothing at all in reply.
t.3.56.17: Then all those ministers, and those citizens of the city as well, saying, "He is not himself," went to their homes, stricken with grief and ashamed.
t.3.56.18: Thus that game of dice went on between Puṣkara and Nala, O Yudhiṣṭhira, for many months, and Puṇyaśloka was ever the one defeated.
